## Status {.unnumbered}

This is a shell, not a released student lab. The previous example numbers and generic computer images have been removed. Do not post the assignment until the actual classroom computer and safe measurement method are documented.

## Teacher setup decisions {.unnumbered}

- Select one classroom computer and record its make, model, and asset number.
- Add a clear exterior photograph of that computer.
- Add a clear photograph of the exterior PSU nameplate. Never open the PSU.
- Decide whether actual input power will come from a teacher-operated wall power meter or verified manufacturer documentation.
- If a wall power meter is used, define the idle condition, the teacher-specified task, the waiting period, and who may operate the meter.
- Choose the branch values used for Questions 2 to 5 and cite the source beside each value.
- Confirm that the PSU maximum output rating is not presented as present wall-input power.
- Test every calculation and write the teacher answer guide only after the actual values are final.

## Calculation design {.unnumbered}

Keep the same six-question progression:

1. Label evidence on the actual computer and exterior nameplate photographs.
2. Calculate branch power from an approved voltage and current.
3. Calculate branch current from an approved voltage and power.
4. Calculate equivalent resistance from approved branch values.
5. Add the approved branch powers to estimate total load power.
6. Compare measured wall-input power with the exterior PSU rating and explain why they describe different quantities.

Use $P_{\mathrm{T}}$ for total power. Keep each GUESS step in a separate row. In Question 5, keep $P_1$, $P_2$, CPU branch power, and motherboard/RAM branch power in separate columns.

::: {.tejwarning title="Safety and interpretation"}
Students must not open the PSU or probe energized internal circuits. A PSU nameplate gives rated limits, not live consumption. A wall power meter reports AC input power and includes conversion losses, so it is not identical to the summed DC branch loads.
:::

## Release gate {.unnumbered}

$\square$ actual computer selected  $\square$ photographs added  $\square$ measurement method approved  $\square$ values cited  $\square$ answers checked  $\square$ student copy tested at Chromebook size

## Google Classroom posting {.unnumbered}

Do not post this shell. Add the final topic, title, due date, evidence list, and one-copy-per-student setting after the lab is complete.
